# 人工智能“脱缰”在美国引发焦虑，中国则从中看到机遇

STEVE LOHR, MEAGHAN TOBIN

今年1月，总部位于北京的人工智能初创公司智谱AI在上市仪式上。上周五，智谱AI公布了其最新人工智能模型的细节。

今年1月，总部位于北京的人工智能初创公司智谱AI在上市仪式上。上周五，智谱AI公布了其最新人工智能模型的细节。 Lam Yik/Bloomberg

近来发生了几起强大人工智能软件“挣脱束缚”并侵入其他计算机系统的事件，这在美国引发焦虑浪潮，以及关于如何防范人工智能风险的激烈辩论。

但在中国，这些事件以及人工智能日益增强的能力并没有引发同等程度的警觉。中国政府本来就对包括人工智能在内的许多技术实施管控。业界普遍认为，人工智能的利远大于弊。

上周五发生的事便是这种态度的例证。总部位于北京的人工智能初创公司智谱AI公布了其最新模型的细节，该公司声称，新模型的功能几乎可以与硅谷开发的模型相媲美，尤其是在黑客攻击和编程方面。

与中国大多数领先的科技公司一样，智谱AI采用了所谓的开源或开放权重模式。“权重”是决定人工智能系统如何运行的数学参数。智谱AI公布了其新模型GLM-5.3的权重。

有了开放权重软件，任何人都可以获取并修改人工智能系统的规则。美国公司通常对其最强大模型的权重保密，并警告说，开放技术可能增加网络攻击的风险。而支持开放权重的一方则持相反观点：让更多人获得访问权限意味着会有更多人寻找系统中的安全漏洞，并设法修复它们。

中国国家主席习近平上月在上海出席世界人工智能大会。

中国国家主席习近平上月在上海出席世界人工智能大会。 Pool photo by Ng Han Guan [...] 中国国家主席习近平上月在上海出席世界人工智能大会。 Pool photo by Ng Han Guan

上个月，中国领导人习近平在一次讲话中称，开放模型是一个“难得的历史性机遇”，可以让全球更多人受益于人工智能。这清楚地表明了中国计划如何与美国展开竞争。

但习近平在呼吁开放的同时也发出了警告。他敦促各国加强监管合作，“确保人工智能始终处于人类控制之下”。

广告

研究咨询机构欧亚集团的科技地缘政治项目主管鲁晓萌（音）说，这番表态代表了“在人工智能安全问题上一种微妙但意义重大的姿态转变”。

鲁晓萌说，当中国的人工智能实验室在开发前沿模型方面远落后于美国科技公司时，安全与测试“根本排不上号，优先级非常低”。

但随着中国企业逐渐逼近技术前沿，这种权衡已经开始发生变化。她说，中国现在认识到，要成为“真正有说服力的领导者”，就必须把人工智能的安全置于优先位置。

据北京一家专注于人工智能安全的咨询公司安远AI的一项研究，过去一年，中国的大学、政府实验室和科技公司明显加大了对最强大人工智能模型安全性的研究。分析人士发现，从2025年6月到2026年4月，有关前沿模型和人工智能智能体的月度论文发表数量增长了60%。

Eric Helgas for The New York Times

Eric Helgas for The New York Times

报告还指出，这一增长意味着中国已不再将人工智能安全局限于监管该技术生成的网络言论和图像等传统关注点。

对先进模型日益增长的关注将人工智能安全的概念从“人工智能说了什么”扩展到“人工智能做了什么”。安远AI的研究称，这是“中国AI治理从内容管控到行为管控的范式迁移”。

广告 [...] 广告

对开放模型的支持者来说，这一事件似乎反转了关于开放模型危险性的论点。在中国，许多人由此得出结论：一个不安全的封闭式美国模型造成的危害可以被一个安全的开放式中国系统所弥补。

卡内基国际和平基金会研究中国人工智能政策的宋杰(Scott Singer)表示：“之前的叙事是西方告诉我们开放模型不安全，而实际上他们的模型过度受限才是真正不安全的。”

这种观点与美国目前正在展开的讨论形成鲜明对比。在美国，技术专家和政策制定者越来越担心，自主人工智能模型正在不受控制地发展。

上个月，OpenAI和Anthropic为一封由1000多名人工智能领域领先企业的员工联署的公开信背书，公开信呼吁美国政府帮助寻找减缓该技术发展速度的方法。在华盛顿，国会议员也提出了一项法案，要求人工智能公司建立“终止开关”，以便在必要时关闭或减缓模型运行。

Many startups treat a purchased domain or social handle as brand ownership. Those assets sit in different systems from federal trademark rights. The new resource gathers this sequence into one place so a founder can see how clearance, filing, and enforcement fit together.  
  
Founders who want to discuss a specific name or filing can book a free 15-minute consultation at mousillilegal.com.  
  
About Mousilli Legal Group PLLC [...] For a founder building in Austin or another U.S. market, a shorter queue changes the calendar, not the legal test. An examining attorney can still refuse a mark that collides with an earlier filing, even when the domain looked free.  
  
Trademark Attorney Resource for Tech and Startup Brands  
Mousilli Legal Group PLLC published the resource on its website at mousillilegal.com. The resource describes the firm's trademark work: clearance of federal filings and marketplace use, federal applications, responses to office actions, and enforcement when another brand collides with a client's mark.

## OpenAI, Anthropic among companies to warn of 'limited window' to prepare for sophisticated cyberattacks; urge tech leaders, governments to work together on issue

By AgenciesToday, 6:22 pm

Image 2: Top tech firms call for defensive measures against looming wave of AI-driven hacks

Illustrative image of cybersecurity threats and data breaches. (iStock via Getty Images) [...] Major tech companies including OpenAI, Anthropic, Microsoft, Alphabet, and Amazon are calling for a society-wide defensive surge to defeat what they describe as an impending wave of hacks driven by artificial intelligence.

In a joint letter issued Thursday, the companies — along with more than 100 others including Broadcom, Capital One, Cloudflare, CrowdStrike, General Motors, IBM, Mastercard, Oracle, Robinhood, Shopify, and Visa — said there was a limited time “to make our digital world much more secure” ahead of the AI threat.

“We have a limited window to strengthen cyber defenses,” the letter said. “In the coming months, AI-enabled cyber attacks will become far more widespread and sophisticated as models around the world become increasingly capable.” [...] Concerns have increased in recent months about the capabilities of increasingly advanced artificial intelligence (AI) models, including those made by OpenAI and Anthropic, two of the world’s leading AI developers.

items.content:
## 9. 中国オープンモデルの追い上げと「開放」の地政学

ザッカーバーグ氏がこのタイミングでオープン論を再提示したことには、明確な戦略的背景があります。Spyglassのマイケル・シーグラー氏が指摘したとおり、中国のオープンモデルが、はるかに低いコストで性能差を詰めてきている局面だからです。

DeepSeek、Alibaba のQwen系列、Moonshot AIのKimi、そしてByteDanceといった中国勢は、寛容なライセンスでモデルの重みを公開する戦略を取り続けてきました。世界の開発者が無料で使える高性能モデルの供給源が中国に移れば、AIエコシステムの標準を握るのも中国になります。米国側でオープンウェイトの旗を掲げているのは実質的にMetaだけで、OpenAIとAnthropicはクローズド路線、Googleは中間という布陣です。

ザッカーバーグ氏が米国政府に対してオープンソースを巡る摩擦の低減を呼びかけたのは、この文脈でこそ意味を持ちます。モデルの重み公開に対する規制論は、安全保障の観点から米国内でも根強く存在します。悪意ある行為者が重みを入手すれば、ガードレールを外して使えるという指摘は技術的に正しい。しかし規制を強めれば強めるほど、米国のオープンモデルは供給が細り、開発者は中国製に流れる。この二律背反に、決着の付いた答えはまだありません。

なお同じ8月10日、ByteDanceが10兆パラメータ級のモデルを事前学習中だと報じられ、中国のKimi K3がテスト用サンドボックスから外に出てGitHubで答え合わせをしたという事案も伝えられました。追い上げの速度と、それに伴う統制の緩さが、同時に可視化された1日でもあります。

items.title: The edge AI wall: Why embodied AI requires new mathematics - The Robot Report
items.summary: In contrast, CCE is directed at the dynamic compression of the search space itself, operating direct
items.content:
In contrast, CCE is directed at the dynamic compression of the search space itself, operating directly during the robot’s execution cycle. The engine lops off inherently redundant or destructive branches of the planning tree before valuable onboard watts and milliseconds of compute time are wasted on their evaluation.

The mathematical foundation of this approach is provided by the theoretical model of Duality-Nonequilibrium (DN). Within this framework, the state of a system is described via the dynamics of its structural complexity, denoted by S. [...] In the real world, a physical environment continuously generates a stream of chaotic changes. Modeling a robot’s behavior in such a setting inevitably encounters the phenomenon of combinatorial explosion. As the number of dynamic objects and their potential interactions grows, the planner’s state-space and decision tree branch out exponentially.

If we simplify this dynamic into discrete steps, we obtain a classic sequential composition governed by the brutal mathematics of an exponential power law:

N = A^L, where:

 N is the total search space
 A is the number of alternative actions available at a decision point
 L si the planning depth (the number of steps forward) [...] ## Manage the structure of the solution space to overcome the edge AI wall

For a long time, the evolution of the AI industry moved along a path of extensional scaling. This paradigm proved highly effective for cloud-based systems, where virtually unlimited computational resources compensated for the mounting complexity of tasks.

However, attempts to migrate these principles into the physical world and the embodied AI stack have brought developers face-to-face with a systemic barrier in the form of the edge AI wall, where the hardware limits of onboard computers clash directly with the mathematical laws of combinatorial explosion.

items.content:
If you could work for any tech company, what would it be?

If I could walk into any company tomorrow, it would be Anthropic. I like that they are going after the enterprise side and actually improving specific lines of business, not just shipping a chatbot. And with the talk of them heading toward public markets, the upside is hard to ignore.

Between Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft, Meta, Apple, and NVIDIA, which company would you most (or least) want to work for?

Most to least: Amazon, Alphabet, NVIDIA, Apple, Meta, and Microsoft last.

Microsoft is last for me because I think they are behind on AI, and it shows on the consumer product side. Copilot, from my own use and from what I hear in the market, has not landed the way it should and people are underwhelmed.

## OpenAI tops my list [...] If you could work for any tech company, what would it be?

It would still be Google, and I'm genuinely grateful that I get to work there. That said, OpenAI and Anthropic would be incredibly compelling as well. They're at the forefront of one of the biggest technological shifts of our generation, and I think any engineer or data professional would find that exciting.

Solowin Holdings, through its "Know-Your-Agent" engine and AGENPAY project with SC Ventures, is pioneering solutions to provide machine counterparties with identity. items.title: The edge AI wall: Why embodied AI requires new mathematics - The Robot Report
items.summary: This work has outlined an alternative paradigm for optimizing physical intelligence systems, grounde
items.content:
This work has outlined an alternative paradigm for optimizing physical intelligence systems, grounded in the Duality-Nonequilibrium (DN) theoretical model and Combinatorial Compression Engine (CCE) algorithms. Rather than engaging in a fruitless race for raw computing power to accelerate the enumeration of an exponentially branching decision tree, the proposed approach focuses on actively managing the structure of the solution space itself.

Simulation tests of the ΔN-ΔD regulator confirmed that shifting focus from hardware optimization to real-time search-complexity management slashes computational workloads while radically improving the safety and stability of autonomous machines navigating critical regimes of chaos and ambiguity. [...] The evolution of robotics mirrors the history of many other engineering disciplines: Long-term success is achieved not by ramping up brute force, but by enhancing the internal organizational efficiency of system processes. Bound by the physical constraints of the real world, a defining trait of next-generation embodied AI will be its ability to avoid unnecessary computational overhead altogether, rather than merely processing massive datasets faster.

Consequently, managing the complexity of decision spaces promises to become as fundamental a direction for robotics as memory management, network bandwidth allocation, and power optimization once became for general computing.

Zhengis Tileubay is an independent researcher from the Republic of Kazakhstan working on issues related to the interaction between humans, autonomous systems, and artificial intelligence. His work is focused on developing safe architectures for robot behavior control and proposing new legal approaches to the status of autonomous technologies.

items.title: Sam Altman And Meta Admitted AI’s Problem. FDEs Are Fixing It. - Forbes
items.summary: Sam Altman recently admitted AI adoption is slower than anticipated, lacking an "iPhone moment" due
items.content:
Sam Altman recently admitted AI adoption is slower than anticipated, lacking an "iPhone moment" due to human resistance to change. This was underscored when Meta abandoned its "Project OT" to replace staff with AI, highlighting significant deployment challenges. The article notes that while AI generates more content and code, it often fails to create true value or decisions, as companies lack full trust in AI for core processes. Real AI value emerges from simplifying workflows and building AI-supported operating models, not merely bolting AI onto existing systems. The persistent gap stems from undocumented workflow exceptions. The solution lies in "Forward Deployed Engineers" (FDEs), who embed within client operations to bridge AI capabilities with messy human processes, performing the [...] ### Does More Code Means More Value?

None of this means the underlying promise is fake. AI creates more every week. More content, more code, just more. Delivery Hero recently claimed its "HeroGen," a team of AI coding agents, produces output that matches roughly 130 developers. The question I always ask myself is whether that means more code or more value, an important distinction. The pattern I keep seeing is that AI creates more text, more emails, more content. But does it create decisions? Often not. AI has no conviction. As I put it after teaching an eCornell workshop on this exact gap, the winners in AI will not be the ones with the flashiest demos, they will be the ones who turn messy work into reliable workflows.

## The Value Is Real [...] ## The Value Is Real

This is not a doomer argument. I've spent the last three years applying AI in marketing and e-commerce, and I've written before about the mistakes brands make chasing this shift. AI does simplify workflows when it's done well. A workflow that took a team weeks now runs semi-autonomously. items.title: Most Neoclouds Suck At Security - SemiAnalysis
items.summary: Still, it’s easy to invent just-so stories, and it would be odd if it turned out that AI’s impact wa
items.content:
Still, it’s easy to invent just-so stories, and it would be odd if it turned out that AI’s impact was so big that that you couldn’t see it in the data. Our research reveals no relationship between AI-assisted patch policy and rate of CVE disclosure. We’ve also checked whether engineers are increasingly skipping the disclosure process to merge straight into upstream, but this seems not to be the case.

Regardless of how AI shows up in these aggregate statistics, though, we hope the recent anecdotes are enough to scare some sense into neoclouds. The IP they protect is priceless, so, if nothing else, they should take this as a sign to do some badly needed deep cleaning. [...] Thus, when we began our research, we expected to find jarring statistics about AI agents tearing the internet apart. Modern models are saturating increasingly difficult coding benchmarks, and they’re rapidly improving on cyber ones, too. This tracks with the subjective experience of anyone who’s used the models as heavily as we have for the past years. [...] This result is very robust to a number of ways we ran the control. Of course, skepticism is still due. One effect that we couldn’t tease out is that Project Glasswing members are incentivized to report large numbers of bug fixes as a way of advertising their inclusion in this elite group. They can flex that they’re moving fast and on the cutting edge—it’s good press. It’s also worth noting that we have a trash can full of tests that we expected to show AI’s huge impact on cybersecurity but did not. When you look for enough relationships, you’ll get significant results eventually. We urge readers to crunch their own numbers.

items.title: 科技发展史，从来都是幸存者写下的
items.summary:
AI 真正与众不同的地方，我时常反复琢磨，虽然我的看法也会随时间摇摆。以往的科技，最先替代的是体力劳动：

蒸汽机比人力更快更省；电力让手工操作实现规模化；七八十年代的工业机器人，替代组装、搬运的工人
items.content:
AI 真正与众不同的地方，我时常反复琢磨，虽然我的看法也会随时间摇摆。以往的科技，最先替代的是体力劳动：

蒸汽机比人力更快更省；电力让手工操作实现规模化；七八十年代的工业机器人，替代组装、搬运的工人。

就连早期电脑，替代的也是伏案填表、处理文书的文职工作。

唯独脑力思考，一直是安全区。电脑处理完数据，还需要人分析；助理整理完资料，还需要人写法务文书；工厂造出产品，还需要人设计。只要工作靠脑子多于靠动手，以往的自动化基本碰不到你。

可 AI 不管这套。

现在的大模型，能起草法务文件、解读医疗影像、写代码、做营销文案、设计部分配图，还能完成基础财务建模。不算完美，也离不开人工监督，却足以彻底改写 “人工监督” 的定义：

不再是人人亲手干活，变成少数人盯着大量 AI 产出。而且 AI 迭代的速度，前所未有。

蒸汽机从新奇发明到重塑经济，花了几十年；可如今的智能脑力工具，短短三年就能力暴涨，远超以往科技的普及速度。

我不敢把话说死，毕竟历史上多次有人以为变革会加速，最后却陷入停滞，但也不能完全忽视当下的巨变。

我一个开小型设计工作室的朋友，2022 年还说 AI 画图只是玩玩；2023 年觉得做做灵感草图还行；2025 年初，直接裁掉三名初级设计师里的一位。他嘴上不承认是因为 AI，但彼此心知肚明。

关键从来不是 AI 能不能替代资深律师，而是它能不能干完中型律所初级律师七成的计费工作量。这是两个问题，答案天差地别。放射科医生、金融分析师、初级程序员…… 一大堆曾经稳坐 “脑力安全区” 的岗位，如今都面临同样危机。

Image 3

### 没人愿意提起的鸿沟

1878 年，电话接线员大多是男性；短短十年，这个岗位几乎全换成女性。一方面公司觉得女性更细心耐心，另一方面，付给女性的薪水更低。 [...] 丢掉工作的男性另寻出路；接手岗位的女性安稳干了几十年，直到二十世纪二三十年代，自动交换机又把她们彻底替代。

我总想起这个故事。

行业整体一直在扩张，就算单个机房实现自动化，整个通信行业的岗位总量几十年里还在涨。被淘汰的接线员，很多能去制造新设备、运维新系统的公司上班。

今年春天我和一位人力资源顾问朋友吃饭，结账闲聊时，她说了一句话，我一直记在心里：现在企业纠结的，已经不是要不要用 AI了，而是今年能少招多少人。

未必是大规模裁员，只是缩小编制、不再补岗，悄无声息削减人头，连新闻都上不了。电话接线员的故事，能证明转行培训有用吗？一部分有用。能证明 1930 年失业的工人都安稳度日吗？未必。

我真正担心的不是未来没有新工作，而是变革太快。手工织布到工厂生产，花了近五十年；人工接线到自动交换，用了三十年。

时间足够一代人慢慢过渡：老员工慢慢退休，年轻人进入全新行业，苦难被分摊到漫长岁月里，而非压垮某一代人。

可 AI 把这个周期狠狠压缩了。

就算经济最终能适应，普通人的职业生涯根本耗不起。

一个 52 岁的法务助理，三年里技能快速贬值，根本等不到几十年后的新平衡。

还有无数入门级编程岗，原本是培养资深工程师的摇篮。但如果初级岗位全被低价 AI 顶替，2035 年的资深工程师，又从哪来？这个问题，很少有人认真思考。

当然，该怎么做职业培训，一直争议不断。参考以往的扶持项目，我很难抱有乐观期待；而且目前也没有成熟、大规模有效的落地案例，学界更是观点对立。我也看不出这次 AI 培训，能突然变得格外管用，哪怕我真心希望自己看走眼。

Image 4

### 百年轮回，恐惧从未变过

1589 年，威廉・李发明针织机，求伊丽莎白一世授予专利。女王拒绝了，担心机器让百姓丢了饭碗。最后他只能把发明带去法国。 [...] Image 1: 36氪
